claim: SUMOylation is a covalent attachment of small ubiquitin-like modifiers (SUMOs) to proteins.
source: The covalent attachment of small ubiquitin-like modifiers (SUMOs) to proteins is mediated by a conserved process known as SUMOylation.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: SUMOylation is a eukaryote-specific post-translational protein modification.

claim: SUMOylation is executed by an enzymatic cascade involving E1, E2, and E3 enzymes.

These data demonstrate that both digitonin (at 20 and 10 μg/ml) and Triton X-100 permeabilise the nucleus sufficiently to allow for SUMO1 labelling of nuclear structures.

claim: RIM1 is a presynaptic active zone protein that is involved in the control of presynaptic Ca2+-channel density, synaptic vesicle priming, and synaptic plasticity.
source: RIM1 is a presynaptic active zone protein that is involved in the control of presynaptic Ca2+-channel density, synaptic vesicle priming, and synaptic plasticity (Calakos et al., 2004; Castillo et al., 2002; Chevaleyre et al., 2007; Han et al., 2015; Kaeser et al., 2008; Schoch et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: RIM1 was recently reported as a SUMO1 substrate.
source: RIM1 was recently reported as a SUMO1 substrate, with additional data indicating that SUMO1-conjugation of RIM1 is required for RIM1-mediated Ca2+ channel clustering (Girach et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: SUMO1-conjugation of RIM1 was reported to be required for RIM1-mediated Ca2+ channel clustering.
source: RIM1 was recently reported as a SUMO1 substrate, with additional data indicating that SUMO1-conjugation of RIM1 is required for RIM1-mediated Ca2+ channel clustering (Girach et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: SUMO1-conjugation of syntaxin1a had recently been reported.
source: With the same methodological approach, we next determined the SUMO1-conjugation status of the SNARE protein syntaxin1a in vivo (Figure 5C and D) because SUMO1-conjugation of syntaxin1a had recently been reported (Craig et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: The biochemical analyses of His6-HA-SUMO1 KI material did not provide evidence for the SUMO1-conjugation of RIM1, syntaxin1a, synaptotagmin1, or mGluR7 in vivo.
source: In sum, our biochemical analyses of His6-HA-SUMO1 KI material did not provide evidence for the SUMO1-conjugation of RIM1, syntaxin1a, synaptotagmin1, or mGluR7 in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: Previous reports indicated the presence of multiple SUMO1-conjugates in synaptosome fractions prepared from mouse or rat brain.
source: Previous reports indicated the presence of multiple SUMO1-conjugates in synaptosome fractions prepared from mouse or rat brain (Martin et al., 2007; Luo et al., 2013), leading to the proposal that SUMO1-conjugated proteins are present at synapses.
evidence: This is stated as background information with citations.

claim: SUMO1-conjugated proteins were proposed to be present at synapses based on previous reports.
source: Previous reports indicated the presence of multiple SUMO1-conjugates in synaptosome fractions prepared from mouse or rat brain (Martin et al., 2007; Luo et al., 2013), leading to the proposal that SUMO1-conjugated proteins are present at synapses.
evidence: This is stated as background information with citations.

claim: RanGAP1 is the most abundant SUMO1-conjugated protein known.
source: SUMO1 conjugated proteins appear typically as a smear of protein bands above 90 kDa (Figure 6, brackets) and as a prominent band at ~90 kDa, which represents SUMO1-conjugated RanGAP1 (Figure 6), the most abundant SUMO1-conjugated protein known (Tirard et al., 2012; Mahajan et al., 1997; Zhang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Digitonin was used to permeabilise cells in order to reduce anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling in the nucleus in several studies.
source: This choice was based on the notion that digitonin preferentially permeabilises the plasma membrane, hence reduces the contribution of the nucleus to overall staining, and possibly unmasks synaptic SUMO1 staining (Girach et al., 2013; Craig et al., 2015, 2012; Jaafari et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as background information with citations.

claim: Digitonin preferentially permeabilises the plasma membrane, hence reduces the contribution of the nucleus to overall staining, and possibly unmasks synaptic SUMO1 staining.
source: This choice was based on the notion that digitonin preferentially permeabilises the plasma membrane, hence reduces the contribution of the nucleus to overall staining, and possibly unmasks synaptic SUMO1 staining (Girach et al., 2013; Craig et al., 2015, 2012; Jaafari et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale with citations.

claim: Limited validation of anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling in neurons may partially explain the widely varying localisation patterns of anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling reported in previous studies.
source: Limited validation of anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling in neurons may partially explain the widely varying localisation patterns of anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling reported in previous studies.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the reasons for discrepancies.

claim: Anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling has appeared as highly punctate in dendrites in some studies.
source: In dendrites, anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling has appeared as highly punctate in some studies (Craig et al., 2015; Martin et al., 2007; Konopacki et al., 2011; Loriol et al., 2013) and relatively homogenous in others (Ghosh et al., 2016; Craig et al., 2012; Kantamneni et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous findings with citations.

claim: Anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling has appeared as relatively homogenous in dendrites in some studies.
source: In dendrites, anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling has appeared as highly punctate in some studies (Craig et al., 2015; Martin et al., 2007; Konopacki et al., 2011; Loriol et al., 2013) and relatively homogenous in others (Ghosh et al., 2016; Craig et al., 2012; Kantamneni et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous findings with citations.

claim: Glycine-induced chemical LTP, stimulation of neuronal activity, and inhibition of neuronal activity all were reported to cause increased anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling in dendrites.
source: Several studies have also shown seemingly paradoxical changes in immunostaining intensity, with glycine-induced chemical LTP (Jaafari et al., 2013; Kantamneni et al., 2011), stimulation of neuronal activity (Craig et al., 2015), and inhibition of neuronal activity (Craig et al., 2012) all causing increased anti-SUMO1 immunolabelling in dendrites.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of previous findings with citations.

claim: Colocalisation is not reflective of the SUMO1-conjugation state of a proposed substrate protein, unless it is demonstrated that colocalisation is lost or diminished when the target lysines of the given substrate are mutated.
source: Finally, with regards to studying specific SUMO1 substrates using immunolabelling, a correlation-based analysis may be of limited use as colocalisation is not reflective of the SUMO1-conjugation state of the proposed substrate protein, unless it is demonstrated that colocalisation is lost or diminished when the target lysines of the given substrate are mutated.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological consideration.

claim: The present findings provide no evidence of the presence of SUMO1 at synapses.
source: In sum, our present findings provide no evidence of the presence of SUMO1 at synapses.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion.

claim: Negative controls for antibody labeling of SUMO1 should be provided whenever immunolabelling conditions are changed.
source: Further, it seems important that negative controls for antibody labeling of SUMO1 are provided whenever immunolabelling conditions are changed, since altering permeabilisation conditions, for example, can have marked effects.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: SUMO1-conjugation of transcription factors can have profound - but indirect - effects on synaptic function.
source: While SUMO1-conjugation of transcription factors can have profound - but indirect - effects on synaptic function (Tai et al., 2016; Estruch et al., 2016; Shalizi et al., 2006), our present data indicate, contrary to previous studies, that the role of SUMO1-modifications in the function of synaptic proteins and synapses remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The role of SUMO1-modifications in the function of synaptic proteins and synapses remains unclear.
source: While SUMO1-conjugation of transcription factors can have profound - but indirect - effects on synaptic function (Tai et al., 2016; Estruch et al., 2016; Shalizi et al., 2006), our present data indicate, contrary to previous studies, that the role of SUMO1-modifications in the function of synaptic proteins and synapses remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Statistical independence was defined at the level of individual animals, rather than individual synaptic puncta or neurons.
source: For the purposes of quantitative immunolabelling, images were taken of 4–6 neurons per coverslip. Statistical independence was defined at the level of individual animals, rather than individual synaptic puncta or neurons (Galbraith et al., 2010), that is, data from individual synaptic puncta and/or neurons were averaged to give a single value for each animal.
evidence: This is stated in the methods section with a citation.
